main_body: Half-timbered house: a large tiled hip roof over plaster walls with timber framing, a front gable porch and a door below it
top_band: Mid-column at x≈47: the roof slope runs from row ~1 to ~43 as tiled brown tones with a lighter ridge/eave highlight. It reads as a sloped top surface. A dark eave line sits at rows ~43-46, then the cream wall face.
evidence: The roof is clearly drawn as a large foreshortened slope with tile rows and a lit edge, and the wall front sits below it. A dark band under the eaves shades the walls. The door and window have dark inset frames, and the gable porch has its own roof slope. This matches the Beodeul house references and is not a flat elevation.

style.evidence: The outlines are dark brown, tinted to the material, which is good. The roof has tile scallops and per-tile highlights, but only about 4 tones against the reference's richer 5-6 step orange and gold ramp. The plaster wall panels are large flat cream areas with no speckle or grain, while the references have speckled plaster and stone texture. The cream panels and timber also make the wall tiles only 2-3 colours each. Next to the references the piece looks flatter and thinner.
